seo.title: Crisis & Safety Resources
seo.description: If you are in immediate danger or thinking about suicide, this page lists where to get help now. This practice is not an emergency service.

hero.title: If you are in danger right now, do not wait for me.
hero.intro: This practice is not an emergency service. Enquiries are answered within two working days, which is not fast enough for an emergency. What follows is where to go instead.
hero.note: Outside Nigeria, use your local emergency number — 999 in the UK, 911 in the US and Canada.

resources.title: Where to get help now

items.name: Emergency services (Nigeria)
items.detail: 112 — the national toll-free emergency number, reachable from any phone.

items.name: Find a helpline — worldwide
items.detail: A free directory of verified crisis lines in almost every country, including the UK, US, Canada and the Gulf. Useful if you are outside Nigeria.

resources.note: If you are in Port Harcourt or elsewhere in Nigeria and need a local service — domestic violence, sexual assault, or mental health — your nearest teaching hospital’s emergency department can direct you, and 112 can connect you to police and medical response.

ifUnsafe.title: If someone is hurting you
items: If you can leave safely, leave. Go to a public place, a trusted person's home, or a police station.
Tell one person outside the household what is happening. Isolation is the condition that harm depends on.
Keep identification, money and a phone somewhere you can reach quickly, and if it is safe to, keep a charged phone on you.
Note that couples counselling is not a safe first step where there is violence or coercion. It can increase risk. Individual support comes first.

ifSuicidal.title: If you are thinking about suicide
items: You do not have to be certain, or in immediate danger, to deserve help. Wanting it to stop is enough of a reason to tell someone.
Tell one person tonight — a friend, a family member, a doctor, or a helpline. Saying it out loud to another person is the single most useful thing available right now.
If you have a plan or the means to act, treat this as an emergency and call 112 or go to your nearest hospital.
Try not to be alone while you feel this way. Ask someone to stay, or go to where other people are.

coveringTracks.title: Covering your tracks
paragraphs: If you are reading this on a device someone else can access, the **Quick exit** button on this page leaves immediately and removes this site from your back button. Pressing **Escape three times** does the same thing.

It does not clear your browsing history. To do that, use your browser’s history settings — or use a private/incognito window, or a device the other person cannot reach, such as a friend’s phone or a library computer.

whenSafe.title: When you are safe
whenSafe.intro: When the immediate danger has passed, there is work worth doing and you are welcome to bring it here. Nothing you say obliges you to book anything.
